clue.text: Strange when ordinary seaman takes the lead

indicators.note: taking the lead means the sailor's letters go in front of the word for ordinary

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the standard abbreviation for a sailor
ordinary means normal, usual

explanation.surface: Something odd happens when a junior sailor is put in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordinary seaman' looks like one naval rank (abbreviated OS), but the two words do separate jobs; 'takes the lead' puts the sailor first.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abnormal departs from the usual pattern, which is what strange describes.

clue.text: Wooden insect?

parts.note: the question mark hints at a word naming both a heavy wooden mallet and a hard-cased bug

explanation.walkthrough: The same word names a heavy wooden mallet used for ramming and a hard-winged insect, so the 'wooden insect' is a tool, not a carving.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a heavy mallet made of timber and an insect with hard wing cases.

clue.text: Attack on TV

parts.note: taken as written
a TV is a television set

explanation.surface: A broadcast assault appears on the television.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is the start or attack of something, as in the onset of an illness or an enemy onslaught.

clue.text: Tome ethan rewrote becoming the worse for wear

indicators.note: rewrote says the letters of the two words are written out again in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone called Ethan has rewritten an old book until it is tattered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewrote' turns TOME and ETHAN into a new arrangement; 'becoming' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Moth-eaten clothes or books are damaged and shabby from age, the condition of something worn out.

clue.text: The French member needed oxygen before performing satire

indicators.note: before means the earlier letters come ahead of the word for performing

parts.note: la is the French feminine for the
an MP is a Member of Parliament
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
a performer on stage is said to be on

explanation.surface: A French politician needs oxygen before going on stage with a satirical act.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampoon is a piece of writing ridiculing a person, a form of satire.

clue.text: Father has sight of cartoon character

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
the eye is the organ of sight

explanation.surface: A dad has seen a figure from an animated film.
explanation.definitionFit: Popeye is the spinach-eating sailor of animated films and comic strips.

clue.text: On the wall she may be barely noticed!

definitions.text: On the wall she may be barely noticed!

parts.words: On the wall she may be barely noticed!
parts.note: a scantily clad glamour model in a poster stuck up on a wall, barely dressed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely noticed' seems to mean scarcely seen, but it means noticed while bare: a glamour poster on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin-up is a picture of an attractive model, often lightly dressed, pinned to a wall.

clue.text: Pair destroying toaster reduced to helplessness

indicators.note: destroying means the word toaster is broken up and its letters rebuilt

explanation.surface: A couple wreck their toaster and are left helpless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroying' scrambles the appliance's letters into OSTRATE, placed after the abbreviation for pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone prostrate is overcome and incapable, as with grief or exhaustion.

clue.text: Still, up to the present time a profit

parts.note: yet means so far, until now
taken as written
a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: Even now, a business has made a profit up to this point.
explanation.definitionFit: Yet again means once more, as still can in 'still another try'.

clue.text: Flat debits placed at random

indicators.note: placed at random says the letters of debits are put in any order

explanation.surface: Debits from a flat-share account are entered haphazardly.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsit is a single rented room used for living and sleeping, a type of small apartment.

clue.text: Scotsman has feature on Welsh town

parts.note: mon is a Scots dialect form of man
the mouth is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A man from Scotland has a distinctive face and is visiting Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotsman' is one word but gives the dialect spelling of man used in Scotland, MON.
explanation.definitionFit: Monmouth is a town in south-east Wales, on the River Wye near the English border.

clue.text: Entire move is fashionable

explanation.surface: Making a complete change is trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'go' is a turn or move in a game, so the whole go is the entire move; the phrase is also an old idiom for being in vogue.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the whole turn in a game, and also popular or in vogue, as in 'all the rage'.

clue.text: Spot agent consuming soup

indicators.note: consuming means the two words swallow the answer within them

explanation.surface: Someone notices a secret agent eating soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Potage is a thick soup, from French cookery.

clue.text: Interfere — start rowing?

explanation.surface: Meddling is like picking up the oar to begin rowing.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means to meddle; read literally, putting an oar into the water is how a rower begins.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to meddle in others' affairs, and literally describes placing a blade in the water to row.

clue.text: Workable type of exam

explanation.surface: A hands-on test can be done.
explanation.definitionFit: Practical means feasible, and a practical is a test of hands-on skill, as in a chemistry lab test.

clue.text: Usually one cannot see the point of this fastener

definitions.text: Usually one cannot see the point of this fastener

parts.words: Usually one cannot see the point of this fastener
parts.note: the sharp tip of this clasp is tucked inside a guard so it stays out of view

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cannot see the point' sounds like not understanding why it exists, but the sharp end is literally hidden in a sheath.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety pin has its sharp end enclosed in a clasp, a fastening device for cloth.

clue.text: One man or another with love

parts.note: Leonard is another man's name
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: One man or another turns up with his sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the first man; 'or another' gives a second man's name, to which O is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo is a man's name, most famously that of the painter Leonardo da Vinci.

clue.text: Keeping payment, a lawyer gets it in advance

definitions.text: a lawyer gets it in advance

parts.note: retaining means keeping
a fee is a payment for services

explanation.surface: A solicitor collects money up front while holding on to the cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A retainer is paid to an attorney ahead of time to secure their services.

clue.text: Type of pain that is constantly annoying

explanation.surface: A kind of ache that never stops irritating.
explanation.definitionFit: A nagging ache is persistent and dull, and nagging behaviour is continual scolding that irritates.

clue.text: Humble churchman going round middle east

indicators.note: going round means the churchman's letters surround the abbreviation

parts.note: a dean is a senior clergyman

explanation.surface: A modest cleric travels around the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humble' is a verb here: to demean someone is to lower them.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to lower their dignity, as humble does when used as a verb.

clue.text: Footballers joined

explanation.surface: Football players have teamed up.
explanation.walkthrough: United is a common name for football clubs, such as Manchester United, so the players are 'United'.
explanation.definitionFit: Many football clubs are called United, and united also means linked together.

clue.text: Dexterous not having a legal claim

indicators.note: not having says the word for dexterous loses the letter given by the next word

parts.note: adroit means skilful, deft
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being nimble-fingered gives you no legal right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not having a' removes the A from ADROIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A droit is a right or entitlement in law, from French.

clue.text: Came together with Georgia the communist

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
taken as written
red is a common term for a communist

explanation.surface: A Georgian met up with a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: When people assemble in one place they gather, meeting as a group.

clue.text: Ninety fish going round do better

indicators.note: going round means the fish surrounds the Roman numeral

parts.note: an eel is a fish
XC is ninety in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Ninety fish circling outshine the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to outdo others, to surpass them in skill.

clue.text: Vegetable sprouting first

parts.note: a green crop whose name is paired with the word sprouting, as in purple sprouting varieties

explanation.walkthrough: The vegetable is known in the variety 'purple sprouting', so the word sprouting comes first in its common name.
explanation.definitionFit: Broccoli is a green vegetable of the cabbage family, often sold as purple sprouting.

clue.text: Appropriate place to keep one's loose change perhaps

definitions.text: place to keep one's loose change perhaps

explanation.surface: A suitable spot to put your spare coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective meaning suitable, but it is the verb meaning to take for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To pocket something is to take it dishonestly, and a pocket is a small pouch sewn into clothing for coins.

clue.text: Drinking-vessel speaker allowed

parts.note: gob is slang for the mouth, which does the speaking
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A talker has been permitted a cup to drink from.
explanation.walkthrough: GOB is British slang for the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblet is a stemmed cup or glass for wine.

clue.text: Go north of the border and come down underground

parts.note: gang is a Scots word for go, north of the border meaning in Scotland
to land is to come down to earth

explanation.surface: Travel to Scotland and touch down in the subway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North of the border' means in Scotland, where GANG means go. 'Underground' is the criminal underworld, not a railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangland is the world of organised crime, the criminal underworld.
